title: Cooperative localization for a GNSS-denied team: UWB ranging, centralized EKF vs covariance intersection, and a spoofed anchor
summary: A stdlib-only simulation of six vehicles with biased odometry where only two keep GNSS. Inter-agent UWB two-way ranging has dropouts, Markov NLOS episodes and gross outliers; optional camera bearings; a lossy, range-limited mesh with a TDMA slot budget. It compares independent dead reckoning, a centralized 24-state EKF at a fusion centre (multi-hop uplink), a naive decentralized filter that ignores cross-correlation, and decentralized covariance intersection, each with plain or robust (gate + Huber + NLOS-aware) ranging. It reports per-agent error over time, NEES and bytes per second, then spoofs one anchor's GNSS with a slow walk-off and shows how far the error propagates with no check, a per-fix gate, peer range votes and solution separation (centralized sub-filters and a distributed per-anchor filter bank).
verified: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06: nominal and spoof scenarios, each range-only and with bearings (seed 1), and 10-seed Monte Carlo for all four; outputs saved in out/ and pasted in README. 20 unittest tests pass; mutations (SS gate disabled, robust weighting disabled) make the detection and robust-ranging tests fail. Synthetic data only: NLOS, comms and odometry models are stated assumptions, no UWB dataset or hardware was used, and none of the related repos was run.
